title: Sliding Window Maximum
spaceBreakdown:
- std::deque<int> dq: holds at most k indices → O(k)  
- std::vector<int> ans: stores n‑k+1 results → O(n) (output, not counted)  
- other variables: O(1)
approach:
When the window moves one step, only the newest element can become the new maximum and the oldest element may become irrelevant.  
Maintain a deque of indices whose values are in decreasing order; the front always holds the current window’s maximum.  
Each index is inserted and removed at most once, giving linear time.
hints:
When the window slides one position to the right, which previously seen element can no longer influence any future maximum?  
k can be as large as n.

Use a double‑ended queue (deque) that stores indices of elements in decreasing value order.  
Example: for nums = [1,3,-1,…] and k = 3, after processing the first three elements the deque holds indices [1] (value 3) at the front.

for i = 0 … n‑1
    while deque not empty and deque.front ≤ i‑k          pop front
    while deque not empty and nums[i] ≥ nums[deque.back] pop back
    push i to back
    if i ≥ k‑1                                            output nums[deque.front]

**Single element** - the array contains only one number.  
`Input: [5],1` → `Expected: [5]`  
⚠️ Bug: forgetting the “i ≥ k‑1” check → returns `[]`.

**All decreasing** - the values strictly drop, so the maximum is always the leftmost element of the window.  
`Input: [9,8,7,6,5],3` → `Expected: [9,8,7]`  
⚠️ Bug: using a max‑heap without lazy deletion keeps stale indices → returns `[9,9,9]`.

**Increasing sequence** - the values strictly rise, the maximum is always the newest element.  
`Input: [1,2,3,4,5],3` → `Expected: [3,4,5]`  
⚠️ Bug: maintaining the deque in increasing order (pop while nums[i] <= nums[back]) → returns `[1,2,3]`.

followUps.q: What if many queries ask for different window sizes k on the same static array?
followUps.a: Pre‑process the array with a Sparse Table for Range Maximum Queries in O(n log n) time and O(n log n) space; each query then answers in O(1) time.

followUps.q: How would you adapt the algorithm when the numbers arrive as a stream and you can only keep O(k) extra memory?
followUps.a: The deque solution is already online and uses at most k indices, so it works directly on a stream without storing the whole array, still O(1) amortized work per element.

followUps.q: Suppose you also need to output the minimum of each window in addition to the maximum, still in linear time.
followUps.a: Maintain a second deque that stores indices in increasing order (monotonic increasing queue) alongside the decreasing one; each step updates both deques and records front values, keeping O(n) time and O(k) space.
